title: activity_event
description: One line in the activity log: a record was created, edited, deleted or restored, with who did it (created_by), when (created_at), which record and, for each field that changed, what it was and what it became. Append-only: the server writes an entry in the same all-or-nothing step as the change it records, and nothing ever edits or deletes it. Personal data is never copied into an entry: for a field marked x_pii in its own schema, and for every field of the sensitive-details collection, the entry names the field and says the values are withheld. Rules the schema cannot express: entries are written only by the server's activity store; nothing can create, update or soft delete an entry through the endpoints; one entry per document write; a write that changes nothing but its own stamps writes no entry.
x_retention: Kept. Never edited, scrubbed or deleted, including when a person is erased: personal values are never copied into an entry, so there is nothing to scrub. The record purge job (P-48) must never touch this collection. (A written policy only; nothing enforces it yet.)

action.description: What happened to the record: created (a new record), edited (fields changed), deleted (soft deleted: the record is hidden and kept) or restored (a soft delete was taken back). Required.

record_type.description: The kind of record, as the registry names it (venue, scheduled_class, individual and so on). Required.

collection.description: The collection the record lives in (venues, scheduled_classes and so on). Required.

record_id.description: The id of the record that changed. Required. Not checked against the collection.

record_label.description: A short human label for the record at the time (its name, title or slug), only when the record has one that is not personal data. Optional.

changes.description: One item per field that changed, in field order. For a created record, one item per field it started with. Optional: a record with nothing to say about fields (for example one restored) has none.

field.description: The name of a top-level field of the record. A change inside a list or object is shown as a change of the whole field.

old_value.description: The value before, written as JSON text. Absent when the field did not exist before, or when the values are withheld.

new_value.description: The value after, written as JSON text. Absent when the field was removed, or when the values are withheld.

values_withheld.description: True when the field is personal or sensitive, so the entry names it but never holds its values.

truncated.description: True when a value was longer than the entry holds and was cut short.

fields_omitted.description: How many changed fields did not fit in the changes list (it holds at most 150). Absent when none were left out.

related_ids.description: Ids to find this entry by: the record's own id plus the ids it points at (a person, a class, a request, a venue, a place). The History button on a card asks for one id and gets every entry that mentions it. At most 12.

id.description: UUID v4, set by the server; also the Firestore document id.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written under (currently 1). Set by the server.

created_at.description: When the change happened (UTC). Set by the server.

created_by.description: Who made the change, as an actor string (user:<id>, system:<name>, web:<name>). Set by the server from the change itself.

updated_at.description: Same as created_at: an entry is never updated. Set by the server.

updated_by.description: Same as created_by: an entry is never updated. Set by the server.

source.description: Where the entry came from: always system, because the activity store writes it. Set by the server.

sequence_ms.description: The moment of the change in milliseconds since 1970, so two changes in the same second keep their order. Set by the server.
